topic: creatives who only use AI for finished output and cannot make it work as a brainstorming, ideation, or storyboarding partner
blind_spots: Little to no evidence on specific tool features or UX changes that would actually enable iterative ideation/storyboarding collaboration; the FIXIT method is referenced but no detail or efficacy data is provided.
No quantitative breakdown of which creative disciplines (writing, visual art, film/storyboarding, music) struggle most as an ideation partner.
Absence of evidence from users who successfully use AI as a brainstorming partner, leaving the success conditions unexamined.
No pricing, accessibility, or learning-curve evidence explaining whether the failure is capability or user workflow mismatch.
contradictions: One source argues AI 'can't be real creative' yet others fear it will 'replace real creativity,' reflecting tension over whether AI is creatively incapable or competitively threatening (https://www.reddit.com/r/aiwars/comments/1ue4dx9/i_personally_cant_understand_the_logic_of_some/).

Promotional/optimistic claims about AI generating large revenue (AI UGC for apps, dropshipping AI agent) contrast sharply with the dominant evidence that AI output is low-quality and requires heavy editing (https://x.com/BrianFrydberg/status/2067266108059504776, https://x.com/fomoliver/status/2062247396633870466).

The motionapp source frames human-AI collaboration as fixable via a method, contradicting other sources that frame AI's creative limitations as intrinsic and unfixable (https://motionapp.com/blog/brainstorming-with-ai-for-performance-advertising vs https://aokistudio.com/50-arguments-against-the-use-of-ai-in-creative-fields.html).
